output:
**What I found:** Move the retry code down. Turn `got` 14's built-in retry back on and delete `src/lib/retry.ts` (the record calls this L4 CODE → L3 LIB). The discount function stays out of bring-down: moving it to `src/shared/discount.ts` keeps the same team as owner, so it's an internal refactor and goes to the architecture skills.

**Why it matters:** By default, `got` doesn't retry POST. Its default retry methods are GET, PUT, HEAD, DELETE, OPTIONS and TRACE, so turning it back on removes the cause of both incidents and 140 lines that needed six fixes last quarter. If you keep the wrapper, your team keeps maintaining code that only repeats what an already-approved library does.

**Do this first:**
1. Turn on `retry` in the shared `got` instance (`got.extend({ retry: { limit, methods, statusCodes, calculateDelay } })`). Move one real consumer off `src/lib/retry.ts` and add a test showing that a POST that fails with a 503 is sent once.
2. Move the remaining consumers, delete `src/lib/retry.ts`, and add a lint rule that bans imports of it.
3. Hand the discount extraction to `morphogenetic-architecture` to decide where it lives.

**What I did not check:**
- There is no source code in the working directory, so this assessment rests only on what you told me. To close it, read `src/lib/retry.ts` and list each behavior it has: backoff, jitter, status codes, error codes, Retry-After, per-attempt timeout.
- I haven't confirmed which call sites turn off `got` retry, or which consumers import the wrapper. To close it, run `grep -rn "retry:" src` and `grep -rn "lib/retry" src`.
- I haven't confirmed the three discount copies are identical, or that nothing else uses them. To close it, run `diff` on the three function bodies and look at `git log -p` for each copy.

---

```
Scope:          One Node.js 22 / TypeScript API repo, one team of four; src/lib/retry.ts and three copies of isEligibleForDiscount
Mode:           Assessment
Decision:       Bring down retry.ts to got 14 built-in retry (L4 CODE -> L3 LIB). No bring-down for isEligibleForDiscount; hand off.
Summary:        retry.ts is 140 lines of generic retry logic with no domain-specific parts, sitting on top of an approved
                library that already does retry and that you have switched off. It costs a lot to maintain (6 fixes,
                2 incidents). got's default method list leaves out POST, which removes the incident cause. The discount
                function is your own policy, and the proposed new location has the same owner, so it isn't bring-down.

Candidates:
- src/lib/retry.ts (outbound HTTP retry with exponential backoff)
  - Move: L4 CODE -> L3 LIB (distance 1)
  - Landing: got 14 `retry` option (limit, methods, statusCodes, errorCodes, calculateDelay, backoffLimit, noise,
    maxRetryAfter), set once on the shared got.extend() instance
  - Owners: API team -> got maintainers (already approved by the platform team)
  - Evidence: 140 lines; 6 bug-fix commits last quarter; 2 production incidents from retrying non-idempotent POSTs;
    every outbound call already goes through got; nothing domain-specific in the wrapper
  - Variation: none reported. Custom backoff curves go in calculateDelay. Endpoints that need a different policy
    set retry options per request. A POST that is safe to retry (for example, one with an idempotency key) must
    opt in per call, not through a global setting.
  - Confidence: High on the move. Medium on matching every behavior until retry.ts has been read.
  - Next action: Turn on retry in the shared got instance, migrate one consumer, and add a test that a failing
    POST is not retried.

Priorities:
1. src/lib/retry.ts
   - Why now: high churn plus a repeated production incident that the landing's defaults prevent
   - Move: L4 CODE -> L3 LIB
   - Landing: got 14 `retry` option
   - Migration proof: one production outbound client passes the retry/no-retry tests and runs through one release
     with no retry-related incidents
   - Retire: delete src/lib/retry.ts and every `retry: { limit: 0 }` / `retry: 0` override; ban imports of the old
     path with a lint rule

Gaps:
- I haven't seen retry.ts. A behavior that got doesn't cover, such as a circuit breaker or a retry budget, would
  have to stay as explicit local code or be judged separately.
- I don't know whether any POSTs carry idempotency keys and really need to be retried.

Handoffs:
- isEligibleForDiscount -> src/shared/discount.ts
  - Reason excluded: same owner (this team, this repo). It's your own discount policy, so it stays L4 CODE.
    This is an internal extraction, not bring-down.
  - Better skill: morphogenetic-architecture (where it belongs: likely a discount or pricing domain module rather
    than a generic `shared/` folder); structural-simplification (confirm that merging 3 identical copies into 1
    simplifies things); architecture-as-code (ban the old copies after the merge). Three identical copies is a
    strong reason to extract, as long as those modules are meant to always follow one policy.
```
